memory_update.content: For AI Layer 3, do not let high-attention reference leaders outrank underfollowed candidates when the underfollowed names have a plausible hidden supply-chain signal and a clear falsification path.

Highest-priority follow-up from this chunk: IESC, STRL, AEIS, UCTT, ICHR, and MKSI. Required next evidence: backlog mix, AI/data-center or advanced-node exposure, customer concentration, margin leverage, and order durability.

Downgrade construction/service candidates if backlog is not data-center linked, if margins are driven by non-AI cyclicality, or if labor constraints prevent operating leverage. Downgrade semicap subsystem candidates if demand is only broad WFE recovery without leading-edge, memory, HBM, or advanced-packaging linkage.
Use VRT as a benchmark for data-center power and thermal infrastructure, not as the main underfollowed discovery candidate.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify data-center backlog, customer concentration, labor constraints, margin sustainability, and whether projects are AI-cluster related.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: No hard evidence in the provided context proving the percentage of revenue, backlog, or operating profit tied specifically to AI data centers.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Electrical contracting and infrastructure services are directly tied to the physical buildout problem that AI data centers face: power distribution, installation, and integration. The Serenity score is high because the signal is hidden inside a services label, but can be tested through backlog mix, data-center exposure, margins, labor constraints, and customer concentration.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Classified as electrical contracting rather than AI infrastructure, so screens focused on chips, GPUs, cooling equipment, or data-center REITs may miss it.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify data-center customer mix, backlog, margin contribution, geography, project duration, and whether growth is tied to AI compute clusters.

ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Site preparation and civil infrastructure could be a practical gating item for AI data-center expansion, especially where grid access, permitting, and construction capacity delay new compute clusters. The candidate is attractive for Serenity work because the thesis is second-order, under a construction label, and testable through backlog, customer mix, geography, and project duration.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: The company is likely screened as infrastructure or construction rather than AI, making any data-center mix potentially underappreciated.

ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Precision power conversion sits inside both semiconductor manufacturing equipment and high-density power-control architectures. If AI-driven advanced-node, memory, and packaging capex remains durable, power-control subsystems may benefit before the signal becomes obvious in end-market labels.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Diversified precision-power exposure can obscure the AI linkage through semiconductor tools or data-center power systems.

summary: Layer 3 ranking prioritizes underfollowed, testable chokepoint candidates one or two steps away from obvious AI demand. Within this chunk, the highest Serenity research priority goes to data-center electrical/mechanical construction and semicap subsystem suppliers where AI demand could show up in backlog, customer concentration, margins, and order visibility. Reference leaders are retained only as anchors and are not ranked above smaller names solely because of popularity.
